issues.text: How the worker as a Linux container (decisions/0134 item 4) changes lane A. Recommended: nothing in REQ-114…REQ-117. Lane A provides what lane B reads: users.is_owner_identity, orgs.kind, orgs.ai_allowed, withPlatform and the audit writer; withWorker, workers.isolation and the claim filter are R2.5. The only lane-A trace of the move is the end of the macOS Keychain for lane-A secrets (О2). Options: (a) no change (recommended); (b) also run the web app in the worker image for local UAT — not needed, `node server/node-main.js` and the docker job of app.yml already cover it.

What replaces the macOS Keychain item `sai-uat-identity` (PLAN M2 owner action, AC2.6) on Windows and macOS. Recommended (a): a secret file outside the repository named by the environment variable SAI_UAT_IDENTITY_FILE (JSON with e-mail and password), read in-process by app/scripts/uat-login.js, which refuses a path inside the repository, a symbolic link or a missing file (REQ-114 c11); the owner keeps it in his user profile folder (on Windows the default ACL of the profile; on POSIX the script also refuses a mode readable by others); the same on both systems, as decisions/0134 item 4 says («environment or secret file»). (b) an environment variable SAI_UAT_PASSWORD — leaks into child processes and shell history; (c) Windows Credential Manager through PowerShell — needs child_process, a second code path for macOS, and the import rules of app/ forbid it. The setup token needs no store at all: `node scripts/setup-token.js` prints it once and writes nothing; Node 22 runs it on Windows and macOS. The session-state file that uat-login.js writes is a secret too: outside the project, deleted after UAT.

What an invited non-owner person may do while G7 is «а». Recommended (a): nothing — the admin cannot create an invite that is not for an owner identity (refused `personal_data_gate`), and an acceptance of such an invite is refused with unchanged state, so no non-owner account and no non-owner personal data exist (decisions/0100 item 2, PLAN §3 G7 default, NEVER-DO 14). Named risk: an owner-identity invite link is a bearer secret; whoever opens it first becomes an owner identity, so the owner accepts his own invites himself at once. (b) owner-identity invites are accepted only in a browser where the platform admin is signed in — closes the risk, more code; (c) allow creating non-owner invites but refuse at acceptance — the person would type a name, an e-mail and a password that are thrown away, worse. Note for the goal: the first real client needs G7 «б», and «б» takes effect only after the consent sentence is released AND the legal pages say «черновик» (PLAN §3 G7); the legal pages are M7 by decisions/0134 item 3, so they should come before the client's first invite (recommended: a small requirement right after M2, not at the end of M7).

How the server knows that G7 is «а» or «б». Recommended (a): one constant in the source (the precedent of decisions/0123 О20 for the public languages), switched by a release through the gates after the owner's «б»; no runtime switch that a stolen admin session could flip. (b) a platform_settings key — needs the check list of 0001 widened and a settings route (M5); (c) an environment variable — changes without a release and without a review.

Where the audit log with the hash chain goes. PLAN puts it in R2.4 (task M2.3), but PLAN M2.2 creates audit_log in 0002 and ARCH §14.5 audits every auth event from M2.2. Recommended: the single writer, the chain, the advisory lock and GET /api/admin/audit/verify in REQ-115 (M2.2); the audit page and GET /api/admin/audit in REQ-117 (M2.3). Option (b): auth events unaudited until M2.3 — a gap in TB6.

AC2.1 needs «the number of cases > 0», but no route of M2.2 (auth only) is a tenant route. Recommended: REQ-115 c7 proves the suite on a planted pair of test-only routes (one correct, one leaking) and REQ-117 c4 requires the real count (at least 2) in M2.3. Option (b): add a small tenant route to M2.2 only to have a case — work for no user.
